purpose: Cross early and split apocope with both labial treatments and isolate delayed wj vocalization.

definitions.FNU: define FNU Ctx([{*i} {*j} -> {*ī} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*w} -> {*u} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]);
definitions.FNS: define FNS Ctx([{*i} {*j} -> {*ī} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [OEAnyConsonant - {*w}] _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [OEAnyConsonant - {*w}] {*w} _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*w} -> {*u} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]);
definitions.FL: define FL Ctx([{*i} {*j} -> {*ī} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [OEAnyConsonant - {*w}] _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [EnglishStarVocalic - EnglishStarShortVowel] {*w} _ .#., OEAnyConsonant {*w} _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*w} -> {*u} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]);
definitions.FNG: define FNG Ctx([{*i} {*j} -> {*ī} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [OEAnyConsonant - {*w}] _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*j} -> {*i} || [EnglishStarVocalic | [OEAnyConsonant - {*w}]] {*w} _ .#.]) .o. Ctx([{*w} -> {*u} || OEAnyConsonant _ .#.]);

predictions.early: Ringe and Taylor 2014 pp. 44–47, 173–174, 238, 246, 250: both vowels disappear before j-gemination; light direct nett/bedd lose the trigger, retained-vowel obliques geminate; heavy rīkiją gives long ī; sarwą gives saru. Ungeminated direct relics support this analysis if independent of later transfer.
predictions.split: Hogg and Fulk 2011 pp. 19–22 §§2.22–24: oral *-az (after z-loss) disappears before gemination; nasal *-ą survives into it. Both secg and here oral nominatives miss gemination, the nasal secg accusative and nett/bedd direct cells geminate, and retaining medial j in obliques is independent of the order. The heavy *ij stems do not diagnose light-stem gemination.
predictions.companions: The paired arms move unchanged SC017, SC112, ordinary final-z deletion and SC041 identically and share the SC111 endingless-aw companion; only the position of nasal loss and its consequent glide treatment changes. A labial sensitivity arm preserves stranded geminated ww+j for existing downstream consumers to distinguish later representation failure.
predictions.door: SC112 before nasal loss sees suffixed dorą; moving it back to its live site exposes short dor and should give dōr. There/where and all lowering identities should be unchanged; these are implementation controls, not historical dates.
predictions.foliation: Campbell 1959 §§576–582 and Ringe–Taylor pp. 46–47: independently test the surviving case endings; a donor stem with a geminate or the searwes-type broken root is necessary but does not show the date or direction of transfer by itself.
predictions.early_ww: Use the identical archived FNS in early position. Its second clause requires a non-w consonant before w, so vowel + singleton wj also escapes and can feed gemination. Contrast the explicitly narrowed FNG.
predictions.geminate_only: FNG adds vowel before wj to the vocalizing contexts. Existing ww preserves j, but ordinary short-V + singleton wj vocalizes. Compare both positions.
predictions.early_delay_wj: Separate sensitivity, not a published early-loss chronology. Motivated by the retained palatal conditioning in Ringe–Taylor pp. 53, 173, 250; delaying singleton short-V wj vocalization allows SC010 to apply to stranded clusters. Expect labial-only effects, unlike retaining nasal a through gemination.
